research.summary: Independent plumbers merchant serving trade and walk-in customers in the SW14 area. Long-standing local business with a solid reputation on Google, but no website at all — everything online rests on the Google listing and an inactive Facebook page. Trade customers and local landlords looking for stock, opening times or a trade account have nowhere to go except the phone.
observations: No website of any kind — searching the name returns the Google listing and directory entries
Google Business Profile is claimed and has genuine reviews
Facebook page exists but hasn't been posted on recently
Nearby merchants and the national chains all have sites showing stock and opening hours
Business appears well established and busy during weekday mornings
problems: Nowhere for a customer to check opening hours, delivery or whether something is in stock
Every enquiry has to come through the phone, which is a job on a busy trade counter
New trade customers have no way to see what the business offers before turning up
Recommendations get searched for and find almost nothing
opportunities: Simple site covering what they stock, hours, location, delivery and trade accounts
An enquiry form that takes pressure off the counter phone
Something to link from the Google listing so searches land somewhere useful
Competitors in the area already have this — it's a gap, not a luxury
talkingPoints: People are already searching for them — the reviews prove it
The phone is doing a job a web page could do for free, all day
Trade customers want opening hours and stock before they drive over
Not about a fancy site — about not losing the people who already looked them up
notes: EXAMPLE DATASET — written to demonstrate the tool, not researched
Independent, not part of a chain, so decisions are likely made by the owner
Best time to ring is probably mid-morning after the early trade rush

script.opening: Hi, is that Kenon? It's Ollie calling from NexalField. I know this is out of the blue so I'll keep it really quick — I was looking at your business online and noticed you don't seem to have a website, and I had an idea I thought could be useful for you. Have I caught you at an alright time for thirty seconds?
script.hook: I build websites for local businesses around SW14. The reason I rang you specifically is that you've clearly got people searching for you — you've got the reviews on Google — but when they find you there's nowhere to see what you stock, what your hours are or whether you deliver. For a merchants that's usually a lot of phone calls that didn't need to happen. Can I ask you something quickly?
script.valueStatement: The reason I noticed you specifically is that you've already got people searching for you and ringing you — that's the hard part and you're doing it. What's missing is somewhere they can land and see what you stock, when you're open and whether you deliver, without tying up your counter phone. That's the whole job really — not a fancy website, just somewhere for the people who are already looking.
script.demoOffer: What I'd actually like to do is put together a quick example for Kenon Plumbers Merchants — your stock, your hours, the area you cover. It takes me about fifteen minutes and then I can show you exactly what I had in mind. If you like it, great. If you don't, no problem at all.

discovery.question: How do customers normally find you at the moment — is it mostly trade who already know you, or do you get new people coming in?
discovery.why: Easy opener and it tells you whether they're relying entirely on regulars.
listenFor: "Mostly regulars" — ask what happens when a regular retires or moves
"People find us on Google" — that's the opening

discovery.question: Do you get a lot of people ringing up just to ask what's in stock or what time you're open?
discovery.why: This is the pain point for a merchant. Let them describe it themselves.
listenFor: Any sigh or laugh here is the sale
"All day" — that's the value statement written for you

discovery.question: Do customers ever ask whether you've got a website?
discovery.why: Lets them tell you about the gap rather than you pointing it out.

discovery.question: Do you do trade accounts or deliveries? How do people normally find that out?
discovery.why: Surfaces the information that's currently locked in someone's head.
listenFor: If the answer is 'they ring and ask', that's the problem in one sentence

discovery.question: Are you looking to bring in more trade customers at the moment, or are you comfortable as you are?
discovery.why: Qualifies honestly. If they're flat out, say so and exit well.
listenFor: "We'd always take more" — move to the value statement
